categories.description: Managed APIs and platforms for building AI-powered applications with hosted state, tools, files, retrieval, execution, memory, identity, and governance.
No/low-code canvases and automation platforms for composing AI application workflows, agents, and tool integrations.
Code-first frameworks and runtimes for building tool-using, stateful AI applications with routing, memory, planning, orchestration, handoffs, and human-in-the-loop flows.
Protocols, action layers, and connector systems that expose data, tools, prompts, and business actions to AI applications.
Evaluation, tracing, debugging, A/B testing, prompt/version management, analytics, and production monitoring for AI applications.
Safety, validation, policy enforcement, prompt-injection defense, moderation, and output constraints for AI applications.

options.name: PydanticAI
options.notes: Type-safe agent orchestration using Pydantic models. Strong validation of inputs/outputs and structured reasoning flows.

options.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
options.notes: Lightweight primitives for building single- and multi-agent systems (agents, handoffs, sessions, tracing, guardrails). Provider-agnostic; integrates with Temporal and supports MCP.

options.name: Claude Agent SDK
options.notes: Production agent SDK built on the Claude Code runtime, with file and shell tools, sessions, permissions, hooks, checkpointing, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP, and OpenTelemetry support.

options.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
options.notes: Direct successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. Combines provider-neutral agents, an agent harness, graph workflows, durable state, middleware, human-in-the-loop execution, MCP, A2A, AG-UI, and Microsoft Foundry integration.

options.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
options.notes: Open-source framework for production agents with tools, graph workflows, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop controls, visual debugging, evaluation, and deployment to Google Cloud. Go 2.0 is now supported alongside Python, TypeScript, and Java.

options.name: Responses API
options.notes: Primary OpenAI API for agentic applications, with streaming, persistent conversations, built-in web/file search, code interpreter, computer use, remote MCP, programmatic tool calling, and multi-agent orchestration.

options.name: OpenAI Assistants API
options.notes: Deprecated hosted threads and assistant runs. It shuts down on August 26, 2026; existing integrations should migrate to the Responses API.

options.name: Anthropic Messages (Tool Use & Computer Use)
options.notes: Structured tool use, input/output text+image, and managed ‘computer use’ for software control.

options.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
options.notes: Google Cloud's managed agent platform, including config-driven Managed Agents, Agent Engine, enterprise search and grounding, tools, A2A interoperability, sandboxed execution, and persistent state.

options.name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
options.notes: Managed platform for prompt agents and hosted code agents, with Responses-compatible endpoints, model choice, tools, identity, scaling, observability, private networking, evaluations, and A2A support.

options.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
options.notes: Managed runtime and services for agents, including browser, code interpreter, memory, identity, observability, evaluations, policies, and registry support.

options.name: OpenRouter Actions
options.notes: Model routing + tool/action execution as a hosted layer for agents.

options.name: LangChain
options.notes: Tool calling, routing, memory, callbacks. Pairs with LangGraph for durable, stateful agents.

options.name: LangGraph
options.notes: Graph-based, interruptible, resumable agent runtime; human-in-the-loop; multi-agent patterns.

options.name: LlamaIndex
options.notes: RAG-first agents, tools, routers, observability; integrates with many vector stores.

options.name: Semantic Kernel
options.notes: Established Microsoft SDK for plugins, connectors, memory, and agent orchestration. Microsoft Agent Framework is its direct next-generation successor; migration guidance is available for active projects.

options.name: DSPy
options.notes: Declarative LLM programming; optimizes prompts/routing for chains & agents.

options.name: Haystack Agents
options.notes: Pipelines + agents with strong RAG and tool integration.

options.name: Temporal.io
options.notes: Durable workflow orchestration used for long-running agent processes. Provides retries, state persistence, and production reliability; often paired with OpenAI Agents SDK or LangGraph.

options.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
options.notes: Open interoperability standard (2024). Enables tool/data integrations across frameworks. Adopted in OpenAI Agents SDK, Responses API, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and more.

options.name: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
options.notes: Open agent-to-agent interoperability protocol for discovery through Agent Cards, task delegation, streaming, and long-running collaboration across frameworks and vendors. Complements MCP's tool and context integration role.

options.name: Agent User Interaction Protocol (AG-UI)
options.notes: Event-based protocol connecting agent backends to interactive frontends, covering streaming messages, tool calls, shared state, generative UI, and human-in-the-loop interaction.

options.name: AutoGen
options.notes: Established conversational multi-agent framework with tool, model, human, and group-chat patterns. Microsoft Agent Framework is its direct next-generation successor; migration guidance is available for active projects.

options.name: crewAI
options.notes: Role-based multi-agent teams, tasks, tools, and process supervision.

options.name: FlowiseAI
options.notes: Drag-and-drop canvas for LangChain/LlamaIndex style agents; REST APIs & auth.

options.name: n8n (AI + Agents)
options.notes: Automation workflows with LLM nodes, tools, and webhooks to operationalize agents.

options.name: Zapier AI Actions
options.notes: Natural-language actions that let agents operate 6000+ SaaS apps securely.

options.name: Langfuse
options.notes: Tracing, datasets, evals, A/B tests, and prompt/version management for agents.

options.name: Weights & Biases (Weave/Evals)
options.notes: Experiment tracking plus eval pipelines and dashboards for agent performance.

options.name: OpenAI Evals
options.notes: Regression tests and dataset-driven evals to guard agent quality over time.

options.name: AgentScope
options.notes: Developer-centric framework with unified interfaces, async execution, sandboxing, and eval tooling.

options.name: Agent Lightning
options.notes: RL training framework decoupled from execution. Supports integration with LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, AutoGen.

options.name: Cerebrum (AIOS SDK)
options.notes: Provides agent SDK, hub, and testing/eval features. Supports deployment, discovery, and distribution.

options.name: Guardrails AI
options.notes: Schema validation, semantic checks, moderation & policy enforcement for agents.

options.name: NeMo Guardrails
options.notes: Rail-spec safety & grounded flows; complements NVIDIA NIM and RAG stacks.

options.name: Rebuff
options.notes: Prompt injection/jailbreak defenses, detectors, and sanitization for tool-using agents.

description: Platforms, frameworks, protocols, evaluation tools, and guardrails for building applications that use AI agents. SDLC-support products such as coding agents, IDE assistants, and PR review agents live in software-engineering.json.
